native_result.query: In which century did the Diversity in Pottery Form collapses and Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases simultaneuosly?
native_result.HypoA: Around 1800 BCE, Diversity in Pottery Form collapses, while Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases.
native_result.HypoB: In the 17th century BCE (raw-anchor transition at the BCE 1800→1700 boundary; calendar-century window BCE 1700–1601), Diversity in Pottery Form collapses (ΔZKeform = −1.870 ≈ 1.89σ_form) while Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases (ΔZkeverz = +1.450 ≈ 1.58σ_dec) simultaneously — the largest such joint event in the BCE 4100–500 in-range span. Derived directly from capital.csv 100-year anchors (ZKeform, Zkeverz), confirmed on time_series_data.csv PotteryForm_inter/PotteryDecoration_inter, and robust at 0.3σ/0.5σ/1.0σ thresholds. Sign convention: CE = −BCE, so BCE 1800 ↔ CE −1800; N-th century BCE = BCE [N·100, (N−1)·100 + 1].
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Align the two files on 100-year BCE bins using capital.csv as the canonical source of ZKeform (Pottery Form) and Zkeverz (Pottery Decoration); verify CE = −BCE by tying time_series.PotteryForm at CE to capital.ZKeform at BCE for all 37 in-range BCE anchors (BCE 4100..500). 2) Exclude the BCE 4300 and BCE 4200 rows in capital.csv because they sit outside the time_series_data.csv coverage (CE starts at −4100) and form a flat −1.13/−1.92 plateau with no transition signal. 3) Compute raw centennial Δ-step (d_ZKeform, d_Zkeverz) at every BCE anchor; jointly evaluate with multi-thresholds ≥0.3σ/≥0.5σ/≥1.0σ using σ_form=0.989 and σ_dec=0.917 from the in-range raw anchors. 4) Confirm with smoothed _inter series that PotteryForm_inter decreases monotonically and PotteryDecoration_inter increases monotonically across the BCE 1800→1700 boundary. 5) Calendar-century labelling convention: N-th century BCE = BCE [N·100, (N−1)·100 + 1]; report the event as '17th century BCE' (BCE 1700..1601 = CE −1700..−1601) following the researcher instruction. 6) Investigate the BCE 1100→1000 case and explicitly EXCLUDE it as a second-order decorative elevation only (ZKeform stays at the −1.13σ collapse floor; no simultaneous form collapse). 7) Rank simultaneous events by |Δform|+|Δdec|; the BCE 1800→1700 event yields joint score 3.32, the largest non-trivial simultaneous event.

The demographic-openness indicator (pollen-based Belau PC1 and its 100-y smoothed variants `pollen_inter_100`, `pollen_inter`, and the 100-y-smoothed cross-site openness `SMOOTH_MEAN_100y`) marks the strongest centennial growth phase on the **1400–1301 BCE** century (the bin labelled `1400 BCE`). The immediately adjacent **1300–1201 BCE** century is the second strongest and the pair forms a coherent growth phase. Three independent growth signals all peak in the 1400–1301 BCE bin:

  (a) centennial mean of `pollen_grate_100` (annual % change of `pollen_inter_100`): +0.00193 /yr — rank #1/10
  (b) per-century linear slope of `pollen_inter_100` vs CE: +0.01152 /yr — rank #1/10
  (c) ΔZ on the 12-indicator capital composite (HatchetSword, Dagger, HouseSize, CopperGold, Amber, MonumentCount, Depot, Sickle, AxesCelts, MonumentSize, PotteryForm, PotteryDecoration) vs the prior 100-y older bin: +0.679 — rank #1/10 (and contemporaneous with the demographic acceleration)

The interior-restricted re-ranking (drops the 2000 BCE and 1100 BCE edge bins; 9 bins considered) yields the **same top-3** in the **same order** as the full-window ranking — full vs interior ranks differ by at most 0 across all compared bins, so edge effects of the 100-y rolling window do not drive the result. The reading is robust.

A cautionary note on what the level metrics say: the absolute openness level peaks at different bins than the growth-rate metrics (`mean_pollen_inter_100` levels at 1200 BCE = 2.04, and `SMOOTH_MEAN_100y` levels at 1700 BCE = 2.58). The 1400 BCE bin is therefore best characterised as a **trough-to-rebound inflection**: openness had been contracting through 1500 BCE (where the centennial contraction is the deepest of the window at −0.0030 /yr) and rebounded through 1300 and 1200 BCE. The "growth phase" framed by the question therefore is the **1400–1301 BCE century** with **1300–1201 BCE** as a closely-following acceleration, jointly spanning the German Bronze-Age groupings labelled **OBA** in the supplied capital periodisation.

(Per the instruction in the plan, the raw `Belau_PC1` series was retained only as a robustness check; raw-PC1 is heavily gappy within this window (≈5–6 non-null yearly samples per bin) so growth metrics derived from it are noisier than those from the 100-y smoothed series. P0||G0.HypoB:
## Stage: RESULT — final candidate

### (1) One-paragraph natural-language hypothesis

In the 100-year time-slice PCA of the 12 forms of capital across the Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE, 5 bins) and Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE, 7 bins) on `data/capital.csv`, **PC1 (43.4 % of total variance; eigenvalue 5.21/12)** captures a sharp polarity between, on its **positive pole**, high **Amber, Pottery Form, Pottery Decoration, Depot/Horticulture storage, and House Size** (loadings +0.40 / +0.38 / +0.38 / +0.33 / +0.31) and, on its **negative pole**, higher **Hatchet/Sword and Monument Count** (loadings −0.36 and −0.27). The phases sit on opposite ends of this axis: **MN PC1 = +2.16 [95 % bootstrap CI +1.75, +2.50]** vs **YN PC1 = −1.54 [−2.50, −0.29]**, a **Δ = −3.70 [−4.73, −2.39]** downward shift along PC1 with non-overlapping 95 % CIs. The per-bin trajectory BCE 3400 → 2300 descends (with a small dip at 3200 BCE) from +2.71 through +2.24 at 3000 BCE, sits at +1.89 in the transitional 2900 BCE bin, then drops to strongly negative values from 2800 BCE onward (most extreme at 2700 BCE, −3.32) and ends at −2.44 at 2300 BCE. PC1 is well-determined (leave-one-bin-out median cosine 0.998, min 0.946 over non-degenerate drops) and identical (cosine = +1.000) whether or not the 12 columns are re-standardised within the analysis window. **The Middle Neolithic is therefore characterised by an Amber-/Pottery-/Storage-/House-dominated capital profile along PC1, while the Younger Neolithic is characterised by a Weapons-/Monument-dominated profile, with PC1 cleanly separating them.**

---

### (2) Supporting evidence

#### 2.1 Pipeline (executed; see `analysis/run_pca.py`)
1. Load `data/capital.csv` with `pd.read_csv(..., decimal=",")` (file uses European decimals; column values are stored as strings without this), drop `group`, `color`.
2. Build 12-row panel = MN rows (BCE ∈ [3000, 3400]) + YN rows (BCE ∈ [2300, 2900]); oldest → youngest.
3. **Re-standardise** each Z variable within the 12-row window (column mean 0, sample sd 1, ddof=1) — main PCA.
   Sensitivity PCA drops this step and uses the file's pooled Z directly (correlation PCA is scale-invariant → identical PCs).
4. PCA via SVD on the standardised 12×12 matrix; `eigenvalues = σ²/(n−1)`. PC1–PC12 (last two ≈ 0).
5. Sign rotation: each PC column is multiplied by −1 when its loading column-sum is negative (after rotation: sum(PC1-loadings) = +1.41 > 0).
6. Bootstrap (n=20 000) of per-phase mean PC1; leave-one-bin-out PC1 stability (skipping the one degenerate drop).
7. Outputs: CSVs and `results.json` written into `/workspace/analysis/`.

#### 2.2 Eigenvalues & variance explained

| PC | eigenvalue | var explained | cumulative |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 5.208 | 0.434 | 0.434 |
| 2 | 2.688 | 0.224 | 0.658 |
| 3 | 1.700 | 0.142 | 0.800 |
| 4 | 1.028 | 0.086 | 0.885 |
| 5 | 0.608 | 0.051 | 0.936 |
| 6 | 0.485 | 0.040 | 0.976 |

Two perfect linear dependencies inside the 12-row window (**ZDolch = −ZSichel, r = −1.000**; **ZKeform = Zkeverz, r = +1.000**) ⇒ effective rank = 10. PC2 captures the ZSichel ↔ ZDolch axis; PC11/PC12 are the two trivial dimensions.

| variable | PC1 | |l| | PC2 | PC3 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Zamber | +0.403 | 0.403 | −0.028 | +0.057 |
| ZKeform | +0.385 | 0.385 | +0.100 | +0.239 |
| Zkeverz | +0.385 | 0.385 | +0.099 | +0.243 |

| ZHort | +0.329 | 0.329 | −0.084 | +0.459 |

| BCE | phase | PC1 | PC2 | PC3 |
|---:|:---|---:|---:|---:|
| 3400 | MN | +2.711 | +1.624 | −2.733 |
| 3300 | MN | +2.059 | +0.195 | −0.923 |
| 3200 | MN | +1.420 | −1.515 | +2.259 |
| 3100 | MN | +2.362 | +0.097 | +0.733 |
| 3000 | MN | +2.239 | −0.403 | +0.879 | ← last MN slice |

**Inputs.** `data/capital.csv` (39 rows, BCE 500–4300 in 100-y increments, 12 Z-variables already pooled-Z; integer `group` labels assign MN to BCE 3000–3400 (5 rows) and SG to BCE 2300–2900 (7 rows)).

2. Select MN rows (BCE in [3000, 3400]) and YN rows (BCE in [2300, 2900]) → 12-row panel.
3. Re-standardise (column mean 0, sample sd 1, ddof=1) → 12×12 Pearson correlation matrix.
4. PCA via SVD; loadings = Vᵀ; PC1 rotated so loading column-sum ≥ 0.
5. Per-bin PC1 scores; per-phase mean PC1 with bootstrap 95 % CI (n_boot = 20 000).
6. Per-variable per-phase means (raw Z within panel).
7. Sensitivity: repeat step 4 without rescaling (correlation is scale-invariant).
8. Leave-one-bin-out stability of PC1 direction.

- `results.json` — machine-readable summary (loadings, scores, eigenvalues, CIs, LOO, redundancy).
- `loadings_main.csv` — PC1/PC2/PC3 loadings.

5. **PC2 = ZSichel/ZDolch anti-correlation; PC3 ≈ ZBeil/ZKeform contrast.** These are **data properties**, not methodological artefacts.

**Stage = result.** Analysis executed, full PCA on the 39×12 Z matrix from `capital.csv` with sign anchored on `ZMonument` > 0 (no actual flip needed: raw loading was already +0.192). All artefacts in `/workspace/analysis/`.

### Numeric evidence

**Variance explained (global PCA, no re-standardisation, n=39, p=12):**

| | PC1 | PC2 | PC3 | PC4 | PC5 |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| EVR       | 0.3184 | 0.2042 | 0.1358 | 0.1047 | 0.0743 |
| Cumulative| 0.3184 | 0.5226 | 0.6584 | 0.7631 | 0.8374 |

**Top PC1 loadings (post sign-flip, sorted by |loading|):** `ZCU_AU +0.399 (Social)`, `Zkeverz +0.381 (Cultural)`, `ZKeform −0.355 (Cultural)`, `ZHort +0.343 (Economic)`, `ZAxtSchwert +0.301 (Symbolic)`, `ZDolch +0.279 (Symbolic)`, `ZBeil −0.261 (Economic)`, `Zamber −0.258 (Social)`, `ZMW +0.237 (Economic)`, `Zhausgr +0.228 (Symbolic)`, **`ZMonument +0.192 (Social, anchor)**, `ZSichel −0.062 (Economic)`.

**Phase summaries (PC1 contrast, 2900–3000 BCE gap excluded):**

| Phase | n | BCE window | PC1 mean ± sd | PC1 min / max | range | slope / slice-step |
|---|--:|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Middle Neolithic** | 5 | 3400→3000 BCE | **−1.430 ± 0.501** | −1.848 / −0.624 | 1.223 | **+0.261** (rising oldest→newest) |
| **Younger Neolithic** | 7 | 2900→2300 BCE | **−1.177 ± 0.367** | −1.621 / −0.645 | 0.975 | **−0.098** (flat-to-slightly-falling) |

Cross-phase delta: mean PC1(YN) − mean PC1(MN) = **+0.253** (modest upward shift).

**Dominant-loading cluster per phase (slice-mean Z × PC1 loading):**
- MN: ZAmber −0.393 (Social) ⟶ ZKeform −0.386 (Cultural) ⟶ ZBeil −0.255 (Economic) ⟶ Zhausgr +0.172 (Symbolic).
- YN: ZBeil −0.299 (Economic) ⟶ Zkeverz −0.271 (Cultural) ⟶ ZCU_AU −0.203 (Social) ⟶ ZHort −0.163 (Economic).

**Robustness check (winsorise ZMonument at BCE=2700 from +3.95 → μ+3σ = +3.00):** PC1 EVR 0.3184 → 0.3241, PC2 0.2042 → 0.2064; loadings all change < 0.002 in absolute value; PC1+PC2 0.5226 → 0.5306. **The structural finding is not driven by the BCE=2700 ZMonument outlier.**

### Submitted hypothesis (natural language)

Across the 39 100-year slices from 4300–500 BCE, the first principal component of the 12 forms-of-capital Z variables (sign anchored so that ZMonument is positive) is a **mixed-domain axis**: its positive pole organises long-distance prestige and settlement-monumentality signals (ZCU_AU, Zkeverz, ZHort, ZAxtSchwert, ZDolch, ZMW, Zhausgr, ZMonument), while its negative pole organises subsistence-economy and pottery-form/amber signals (ZKeform, ZBeil, Zamber, ZSichel). PC1 captures 31.8% of the variance (PC1+PC2 = 52.3%).

The **Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE)** occupies the deeper-negative side of this axis (mean PC1 = −1.43 ± 0.50; range −1.85 to −0.62), with the trajectory plunging from PC1 ≈ −0.62 at 3400 BCE to a phase minimum of −1.85 at 3200 BCE and oscillating around −1.5 to −1.8 for 3200–3000 BCE. This phase is dominantly **pulled-negative by peak amber networks (ZAmber > +1.4 throughout), peak pottery-form elaboration (ZKeform ≈ +1.0 σ), and peak celt/axe-tool use (ZBeil ≈ +1.0 σ)**, with a small positive offset from slightly larger houses (Zhausgr). The MN phase is **NOT a period of intensified monumentality or symbolic weaponry** — those variables move only modestly — but of intensified **long-distance exchange coupled with specialised craft elaboration**.

The **Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE)** sits on the **less-negative same lobe** of PC1 (mean −1.18 ± 0.37; range −1.62 to −0.65), with a flat-to-slightly-falling trajectory (slope ≈ −0.10 / 100-yr slice-step). The dominant-loading cluster is now **economic**: continued high celt/axe-tool use keeps PC1 negative, while **prestige-exchange and storage markers collapse** (ZCU_AU ≈ −0.5, ZHort ≈ −0.5) and **pottery decoration elaboration retreats** (Zkeverz ≈ −0.7). Net, YN keeps the **utilitarian-tool pole** of MN but lets go of long-distance prestige, pottery-finish elaboration, and depot accumulation.

**Phase shift MN → YN:** PC1 mean rises modestly by +0.253, but the move is dominated by a **contraction of the prestige/network pole** (amber, copper-gold, pottery-decoration, depot storage all attenuate) rather than by a fundamental axis flip. Both phases remain on the negative lobe of PC1, with MN roughly 0.7σ (in PC1 s.d. units averaged across slices) deeper-negative than YN. The qualitative findings are **robust to the BCE=2700 ZMonument outlier** (ZMonument = +3.95 σ), which on its own changes PC1 EVR by < 1 pp and does not disturb the loading cluster.

### Workflow summary

1. Parsed `capital.csv` after substituting decimal commas inside quoted cells with dots (file uses `\r\n` line endings and decimal commas; standard `pd.read_csv` follows).

### Submitted hypothesis (natural language)

Across the 39 100-year slices from 4300–500 BCE, the first principal component of the 12 forms-of-capital Z variables (sign anchored so that ZMonument is positive) is a **mixed-domain axis**: its positive pole organises long-distance prestige and settlement-monumentality signals (ZCU_AU, Zkeverz, ZHort, ZAxtSchwert, ZDolch, ZMW, Zhausgr, ZMonument), while its negative pole organises subsistence-economy and pottery-form/amber signals (ZKeform, ZBeil, Zamber, ZSichel). PC1 captures 31.8% of the variance (PC1+PC2 = 52.3%).

The **Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE)** occupies the deeper-negative side of this axis (mean PC1 = −1.43 ± 0.50; range −1.85 to −0.62), with the trajectory plunging from PC1 ≈ −0.62 at 3400 BCE to a phase minimum of −1.85 at 3200 BCE and oscillating around −1.5 to −1.8 for 3200–3000 BCE. This phase is dominantly **pulled-negative by peak amber networks (ZAmber > +1.4 throughout), peak pottery-form elaboration (ZKeform ≈ +1.0 σ), and peak celt/axe-tool use (ZBeil ≈ +1.0 σ)**, with a small positive offset from slightly larger houses (Zhausgr). The MN phase is **NOT a period of intensified monumentality or symbolic weaponry** — those variables move only modestly — but of intensified **long-distance exchange coupled with specialised craft elaboration**.

The **Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE)** sits on the **less-negative same lobe** of PC1 (mean −1.18 ± 0.37; range −1.62 to −0.65), with a flat-to-slightly-falling trajectory (slope ≈ −0.10 / 100-yr slice-step). The dominant-loading cluster is now **economic**: continued high celt/axe-tool use keeps PC1 negative, while **prestige-exchange and storage markers collapse** (ZCU_AU ≈ −0.5, ZHort ≈ −0.5) and **pottery decoration elaboration retreats** (Zkeverz ≈ −0.7). Net, YN keeps the **utilitarian-tool pole** of MN but lets go of long-distance prestige, pottery-finish elaboration, and depot accumulation.

**Phase shift MN → YN:** PC1 mean rises modestly by +0.253, but the move is dominated by a **contraction of the prestige/network pole** (amber, copper-gold, pottery-decoration, depot storage all attenuate) rather than by a fundamental axis flip. Both phases remain on the negative lobe of PC1, with MN roughly 0.7σ (in PC1 s.d. units averaged across slices) deeper-negative than YN. The qualitative findings are **robust to the BCE=2700 ZMonument outlier** (ZMonument = +3.95 σ), which on its own changes PC1 EVR by < 1 pp and does not disturb the loading cluster.

1. Parsed `capital.csv` after substituting decimal commas inside quoted cells with dots (file uses `\r\n` line endings and decimal commas; standard `pd.read_csv` follows).
2. Verified each of the 12 Z columns is already pre-standardised (mean ≈ 0 within 1e-3, sd ≈ 1 within 1e-2; sum of variances ≈ 11.24) — **no re-standardisation** before PCA. Documented in the no-op step.
3. Global PCA via `np.linalg.eigh` on the (n−1)-normalised covariance, **option (b)** — option (a) per-slice PCA is undefined because each 100-year slice has n=1.
4. Anchored PC1 sign so loading on **ZMonument** is positive (raw loading already +0.192, no flip performed; `anchor_sign` returns +1.0).

6. Reported per-phase mean ± sd, range, slope vs chronological index, and the **dominant-loading cluster** as slice-mean-Z × PC1-loading (a contribution measure that simultaneously encodes the slice's capital mix and PC1's polarity).
7. Robustness: replaced ZMonument at BCE=2700 with μ+3σ (=+3.00) and re-ran PCA — variance + loadings were unchanged within rounding.

### Limitations / call-outs

- **PC1 captures 32% of variance**, with PC2 contributing another 20%; reading the phases purely in PC1 understates complexity (especially YN's PC1/PC2 joint read).
- **ZMonument anchor was relatively weak** in this dataset (loading +0.192, the second-smallest absolute loading on PC1). ### Submitted hypothesis (natural language)

Across the 39 100-year slices from 4300–500 BCE, the first principal component of the 12 forms-of-capital Z variables (sign anchored so that ZMonument is positive) is a **mixed-domain axis**: its positive pole organises long-distance prestige and settlement-monumentality signals (ZCU_AU, Zkeverz, ZHort, ZAxtSchwert, ZDolch, ZMW, Zhausgr, ZMonument), while its negative pole organises subsistence-economy and pottery-form/amber signals (ZKeform, ZBeil, Zamber, ZSichel). PC1 captures 31.8% of the variance (PC1+PC2 = 52.3%).

The **Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE)** occupies the deeper-negative side of this axis (mean PC1 = −1.43 ± 0.50; range −1.85 to −0.62), with the trajectory plunging from PC1 ≈ −0.62 at 3400 BCE to a phase minimum of −1.85 at 3200 BCE and oscillating around −1.5 to −1.8 for 3200–3000 BCE. This phase is dominantly **pulled-negative by peak amber networks (ZAmber > +1.4 throughout), peak pottery-form elaboration (ZKeform ≈ +1.0 σ), and peak celt/axe-tool use (ZBeil ≈ +1.0 σ)**, with a small positive offset from slightly larger houses (Zhausgr). The MN phase is **NOT a period of intensified monumentality or symbolic weaponry** — those variables move only modestly — but of intensified **long-distance exchange coupled with specialised craft elaboration**.

The **Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE)** sits on the **less-negative same lobe** of PC1 (mean −1.18 ± 0.37; range −1.62 to −0.65), with a flat-to-slightly-falling trajectory (slope ≈ −0.10 / 100-yr slice-step). The dominant-loading cluster is now **economic**: continued high celt/axe-tool use keeps PC1 negative, while **prestige-exchange and storage markers collapse** (ZCU_AU ≈ −0.5, ZHort ≈ −0.5) and **pottery decoration elaboration retreats** (Zkeverz ≈ −0.7). Net, YN keeps the **utilitarian-tool pole** of MN but lets go of long-distance prestige, pottery-finish elaboration, and depot accumulation.

**Phase shift MN → YN:** PC1 mean rises modestly by +0.253, but the move is dominated by a **contraction of the prestige/network pole** (amber, copper-gold, pottery-decoration, depot storage all attenuate) rather than by a fundamental axis flip. Both phases remain on the negative lobe of PC1, with MN roughly 0.7σ (in PC1 s.d. units averaged across slices) deeper-negative than YN. The qualitative findings are **robust to the BCE=2700 ZMonument outlier** (ZMonument = +3.95 σ), which on its own changes PC1 EVR by < 1 pp and does not disturb the loading cluster.

### Workflow summary

1. Parsed `capital.csv` after substituting decimal commas inside quoted cells with dots (file uses `\r\n` line endings and decimal commas; standard `pd.read_csv` follows).
2. Verified each of the 12 Z columns is already pre-standardised (mean ≈ 0 within 1e-3, sd ≈ 1 within 1e-2; sum of variances ≈ 11.24) — **no re-standardisation** before PCA. Documented in the no-op step.
3. Global PCA via `np.linalg.eigh` on the (n−1)-normalised covariance, **option (b)** — option (a) per-slice PCA is undefined because each 100-year slice has n=1.
4. Anchored PC1 sign so loading on **ZMonument** is positive (raw loading already +0.192, no flip performed; `anchor_sign` returns +1.0).

6. Reported per-phase mean ± sd, range, slope vs chronological index, and the **dominant-loading cluster** as slice-mean-Z × PC1-loading (a contribution measure that simultaneously encodes the slice's capital mix and PC1's polarity).

## Result — PC1 characterisation of the 12 capital Z‑variables per 100‑yr slice, applied to Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE)

### Natural‑language hypothesis (submission answer)

**The first principal component of the 12 capital Z‑variables (PC1, ≈30% of total variance) is an axis that contrasts the metal/ornament/ritual‑deposit complex (Copper+Gold, Pottery decoration, Depot hoards, Battle axes+Swords, Daggers — all loading ≈ +0.51 to +0.78) against the utilitarian domestic‑craft complex (Pottery form, Axes+Celts, Amber, Sickle — loadings −0.29 to −0.67). Both Neolithic phases sit firmly on the −PC1 (utilitarian‑craft) side of the axis but at different depths: the Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE, 5 slices) carries PC1 mean = −2.62 ± 0.93 sd (median −2.80, range [−3.40 at 3000 BCE, −1.11 at 3400 BCE]), and the Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE, 7 slices = group SG) carries PC1 mean = −2.13 ± 0.82 sd (median −2.32, range [−3.05 at 2800 BCE, −0.79 at 2300 BCE]). The Younger Neolithic is therefore *moderately less utilitarian / more metal‑+‑ornament‑+‑deposit‑oriented* than the Middle Neolithic (Δmean ≈ +0.49 on the oriented PC1 scale; Welch t = −0.94, p ≈ 0.37, not significant given n=5 vs n=7), with its least‑utilitarian century being the latest one (2400–2300 BCE), while the Middle Neolithic is most strongly utilitarian in the middle of its window (3200–3000 BCE).**

### Workflow (executed)

1. **Source of truth:** `data/capital.csv` (39 × 12, all cells non‑NaN, German comma decimals handled with `decimal=","`); consistency against `data/time_series_data.csv` confirmed (max diff 0.0 at every century BCE).
2. **Time grid:** 39 century slices from 4300 BCE to 500 BCE. MN = {3400, 3300, 3200, 3100, 3000}; Younger/SG = {2900, 2800, 2700, 2600, 2500, 2400, 2300}. Closed, disjoint, adjacent intervals aligned to the centennial grid.
3. **Standardisation:** each of the 12 Z‑columns centred to mean 0, sd 1 across the 39 rows.
4. **PCA:** eigendecomposition of the 12 × 12 correlation matrix (`np.linalg.eigh`). PC1 extracted (λ₁ = 3.639). Loadings = √λ · eigenvector, oriented so the variable with the largest absolute loading (ZCU_AU, |l| = 0.777) is positive; the alternative raw sign is also saved (PC1_raw column) so the result is sign‑transparent.
5. **Per‑slice PC1 score:** score = standardised Z‑columns · oriented loadings; produced for all 39 slices.
6. **Phase characterisation:** mean ± sd (primary), median (IQR), min/max (robustness), per‑slice table for MN and Younger/SG, Welch t‑test for the phase contrast, Spearman ρ of each Z‑column with PC1 for cross‑sanity.

| PC | eigenvalue | variance | cumulative |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3.639 | **30.33 %** | 30.33 % |
| 2 | 2.336 | 19.47 % | **49.79 %** |
| 3 | 1.548 | 12.90 % | 62.70 % |
| 4 | 1.500 | 12.50 % | 75.19 % |
| 5…12 | 0.878 … 0.033 | ⇣ | 100 % |

**PC1 loadings (oriented, largest |loading| positive; raw sign also reported)**

| Variable | Label | loading (oriented) | sign raw |

### Evidence (counts and tables)

- capital.csv loaded as **39 rows × 15 cols**; 12 Z‑cols required, all complete (NaN counts: 0 for each).
- BCE grid: 500, 600, … 4300 (39 unique values, 100‑year spacing).
- MN group (in `capital.csv` `group` column) = {3400, 3300, 3200, 3100, 3000}; Younger group = SG = {2900, 2800, 2700, 2600, 2500, 2400, 2300}; verified that `group` labels map onto the question's window definitions 1:1.
- Cross‑source consistency: at each of the 39 century BCE years, max absolute difference between `capital.csv` Z‑cols and `time_series_data.csv` `*` and `*_inter` cols = 0.0.
- `time_series_data.csv` provides no pre‑computed 100‑yr smoothed / detrended / growth‑rate columns for the 12 capital variables (only the raw Z and a piecewise‑constant forward‑fill `_inter` are present), so nothing could substitute for the fresh centennial PCA.
- PC1 explains **30.33 %** of total variance (λ₁ = 3.639 / sum λ = 12); PC1+PC2 = 49.79 %; first 4 components retain 75.19 %.
- Spearman ρ of each Z‑column with PC1_oriented score (sanity check on the loadings): all variables with positive PC1_oriented loadings have ρ > 0 (Hatchets+Swords +0.75, Daggers +0.79, Copper+Gold +0.76, Monument size +0.63, Monument count +0.51, House size +0.43, Depot +0.60, Pottery decoration +0.57), and the negatively loaded variables trend negative (Amber −0.42, Pottery form −0.66, Axes+Celts −0.30); Sickle's ρ is near zero (+0.06), consistent with its small loading.

### Limitations / honest caveats

1. **One component, one sign convention.** PC1 is only determined up to a global sign; I chose "largest |loading| positive" (so ZCU_AU = +0.777 is the dominant +PC1 indicator). The raw‑sign scores are also saved (`per_slice_PC1_signs.csv`); the MN vs YN contrast is small and the *direction* flips under the alternative sign.
2. **Small slice counts.** Only 5 (MN) and 7 (Younger/SG) slices enter the phase means; the Welch t = −0.94, p = 0.37, so the apparent MN→Younger shift toward metal/ornament/deposit capital (+0.49 on PC1_oriented) is not significant. The description still rests on the qualitative loading direction, not on inferential claims of "different levels".
3. **PCA over 39 slices.** The PC1 vector was estimated on the *full* centennial grid (4300–500 BCE), so the MN and Younger windows are not held out; their mean PC1 is a within‑sample score, not a leave‑one‑out estimate. Resampling the PC1 fit on the two phases alone would shift the eigenvector slightly.
4. **No imputation, no smoothing.** capital.csv has no missing Z‑values; no growth rates, no 100‑yr rolling means of the capital Z‑values were computed. Centennial aggregation is the natural granularity for "100‑year time slices"; sub‑century yearly values are mostly step‑functions in the supplied data and would not change the result.
5. **Variable name map (`SG` ↔ "Younger Neolithic").** The dataset labels 2900–2300 BCE as `SG`, not `YN`; I treat the two as synonymous per the researcher's confirmation.
6. **Sign convention flips the "complexity direction".** Under the unsigned eigendecomposition MN sits at +2.62 and Younger/SG at +2.13 (MN slightly *more* positive); under the "largest |loading| positive" convention MN sits at −2.62 and Younger/SG at −2.13 (MN slightly *less* positive). The qualitative loading story — metal/ornament/deposit vs domestic craft — is the same in both signs; only the labeling of "+" and "−" flips.

### Natural‑language hypothesis (submission answer)

**The first principal component of the 12 capital Z‑variables (PC1, ≈30% of total variance) is an axis that contrasts the metal/ornament/ritual‑deposit complex (Copper+Gold, Pottery decoration, Depot hoards, Battle axes+Swords, Daggers — all loading ≈ +0.51 to +0.78) against the utilitarian domestic‑craft complex (Pottery form, Axes+Celts, Amber, Sickle — loadings −0.29 to −0.67). Both Neolithic phases sit firmly on the −PC1 (utilitarian‑craft) side of the axis but at different depths: the Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE, 5 slices) carries PC1 mean = −2.62 ± 0.93 sd (median −2.80, range [−3.40 at 3000 BCE, −1.11 at 3400 BCE]), and the Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE, 7 slices = group SG) carries PC1 mean = −2.13 ± 0.82 sd (median −2.32, range [−3.05 at 2800 BCE, −0.79 at 2300 BCE]). The Younger Neolithic is therefore *moderately less utilitarian / more metal‑+‑ornament‑+‑deposit‑oriented* than the Middle Neolithic (Δmean ≈ +0.49 on the oriented PC1 scale; Welch t = −0.94, p ≈ 0.37, not significant given n=5 vs n=7), with its least‑utilitarian century being the latest one (2400–2300 BCE), while the Middle Neolithic is most strongly utilitarian in the middle of its window (3200–3000 BCE).**

### Workflow (executed)

1. **Source of truth:** `data/capital.csv` (39 × 12, all cells non‑NaN, German comma decimals handled with `decimal=","`); consistency against `data/time_series_data.csv` confirmed (max diff 0.0 at every century BCE).
2. **Time grid:** 39 century slices from 4300 BCE to 500 BCE. MN = {3400, 3300, 3200, 3100, 3000}; Younger/SG = {2900, 2800, 2700, 2600, 2500, 2400, 2300}. Closed, disjoint, adjacent intervals aligned to the centennial grid.
3. **Standardisation:** each of the 12 Z‑columns centred to mean 0, sd 1 across the 39 rows.
4. **PCA:** eigendecomposition of the 12 × 12 correlation matrix (`np.linalg.eigh`). PC1 extracted (λ₁ = 3.639). Loadings = √λ · eigenvector, oriented so the variable with the largest absolute loading (ZCU_AU, |l| = 0.777) is positive; the alternative raw sign is also saved (PC1_raw column) so the result is sign‑transparent.
5. **Per‑slice PC1 score:** score = standardised Z‑columns · oriented loadings; produced for all 39 slices.
6. **Phase characterisation:** mean ± sd (primary), median (IQR), min/max (robustness), per‑slice table for MN and Younger/SG, Welch t‑test for the phase contrast, Spearman ρ of each Z‑column with PC1 for cross‑sanity.

| 2 | 2.336 | 19.47 % | **49.79 %** |

One‑line semantic read of the **+PC1 pole**: a metal‑rich, ornament‑rich, ritual‑deposit signature (Copper+Gold, decorated pottery, hoard/depot finds, weapons). The **−PC1 pole** is a domestic‑craft signature (plain pottery forms, axes & celts, amber, sickles).

Welch two‑sample t‑test on PC1_oriented (MN vs Younger SG): **t = −0.942, p = 0.374, Δmean(MN − YG) = −0.490** (n = 5 vs 7). The MN→Younger shift is in the direction of *less* utilitarian / *more* metal+ornament+deposit but is not statistically distinguishable from noise at these slice counts.

### Evidence (counts and tables)

- capital.csv loaded as **39 rows × 15 cols**; 12 Z‑cols required, all complete (NaN counts: 0 for each).
- BCE grid: 500, 600, … 4300 (39 unique values, 100‑year spacing).

- Cross‑source consistency: at each of the 39 century BCE years, max absolute difference between `capital.csv` Z‑cols and `time_series_data.csv` `*` and `*_inter` cols = 0.0.
- `time_series_data.csv` provides no pre‑computed 100‑yr smoothed / detrended / growth‑rate columns for the 12 capital variables (only the raw Z and a piecewise‑constant forward‑fill `_inter` are present), so nothing could substitute for the fresh centennial PCA.
- PC1 explains **30.33 %** of total variance (λ₁ = 3.639 / sum λ = 12); PC1+PC2 = 49.79 %; first 4 components retain 75.19 %.
- Spearman ρ of each Z‑column with PC1_oriented score (sanity check on the loadings): all variables with positive PC1_oriented loadings have ρ > 0 (Hatchets+Swords +0.75, Daggers +0.79, Copper+Gold +0.76, Monument size +0.63, Monument count +0.51, House size +0.43, Depot +0.60, Pottery decoration +0.57), and the negatively loaded variables trend negative (Amber −0.42, Pottery form −0.66, Axes+Celts −0.30); Sickle's ρ is near zero (+0.06), consistent with its small loading.

### Limitations / honest caveats

1. **One component, one sign convention.** PC1 is only determined up to a global sign; I chose "largest |loading| positive" (so ZCU_AU = +0.777 is the dominant +PC1 indicator). The raw‑sign scores are also saved (`per_slice_PC1_signs.csv`); the MN vs YN contrast is small and the *direction* flips under the alternative sign.
2. **Small slice counts.** Only 5 (MN) and 7 (Younger/SG) slices enter the phase means; the Welch t = −0.94, p = 0.37, so the apparent MN→Younger shift toward metal/ornament/deposit capital (+0.49 on PC1_oriented) is not significant. The description still rests on the qualitative loading direction, not on inferential claims of "different levels".
3. **PCA over 39 slices.** The PC1 vector was estimated on the *full* centennial grid (4300–500 BCE), so the MN and Younger windows are not held out; their mean PC1 is a within‑sample score, not a leave‑one‑out estimate. Resampling the PC1 fit on the two phases alone would shift the eigenvector slightly.
4. **No imputation, no smoothing.** capital.csv has no missing Z‑values; no growth rates, no 100‑yr rolling means of the capital Z‑values were computed. Centennial aggregation is the natural granularity for "100‑year time slices"; sub‑century yearly values are mostly step‑functions in the supplied data and would not change the result.
5. **Variable name map (`SG` ↔ "Younger Neolithic").** The dataset labels 2900–2300 BCE as `SG`, not `YN`; I treat the two as synonymous per the researcher's confirmation.
6. **Sign convention flips the "complexity direction".** Under the unsigned eigendecomposition MN sits at +2.62 and Younger/SG at +2.13 (MN slightly *more* positive); under the "largest |loading| positive" convention MN sits at −2.62 and Younger/SG at −2.13 (MN slightly *less* positive). 3. **PCA over 39 slices.** The PC1 vector was estimated on the *full* centennial grid (4300–500 BCE), so the MN and Younger windows are not held out; their mean PC1 is a within‑sample score, not a leave‑one‑out estimate. Resampling the PC1 fit on the two phases alone would shift the eigenvector slightly.
4. **No imputation, no smoothing.** capital.csv has no missing Z‑values; no growth rates, no 100‑yr rolling means of the capital Z‑values were computed. native_result.HypoB:
## Result — PC1 characterization of Middle vs. Younger Neolithic

### Concise working flow (executed; see `artifacts/analysis.py`)
1. Load `capital.csv` (39 centennial slices BCE 4300–500; 12 Z-valued capital variables + colour/group metadata). Decimal separator `,` recognised.
2. Re-standardise the 12 variables to mean 0 / SD 1 across the 39 slices (negligible rescaling since the supplied values are already ≈Z-scored, except `ZSichel` whose input SD ≈ 0.54, retained as a caveat).
3. Compute the joint correlation-matrix PCA on the 39 × 12 matrix. Extract PC1–PC12; orientation rule: sign PC1 such that the sum of all 12 loadings is positive. (Sensitivity: a covariance-matrix PCA, included; loadings essentially identical, PC1 explained variance 31.8% vs 30.3% on correlation.)
4. Score the 39 slices via `Z @ loadings`. Aggregate per-phase means, medians, SDs, ranges, linear trends, and per-domain Z averages.
5. Decompose per-variable contributions to the phase-mean PC1 scores.
6. Supplementary cross-correlation: align the 12 BCE marks (3400–2300) to `pollen_openness_score_*.csv` and correlate PC1 with `SMOOTH_MEAN_100y` (primary) plus seven other openness series.
7. Sanity check: project `time_series_data.csv` per-year `*_inter` columns onto the PC1 loading vector; show that at the 12 BCE marks the projection matches the centennial score to machine precision.
8. Persist all tables and a `analysis_summary.json` under `/workspace/artifacts/`.

### Key numerical evidence

PC1 (correlation, primary) — explained variance:
- PC1: 30.3%; PC2: 19.5%; PC3: 12.9%; (PC1–PC3 cumulative: 62.7%)

PC1 loadings, oriented sum>0 (variable : PC1 loading : domain):
- ZAxtSchwert +0.299 — Symbolic
- ZDolch      +0.266 — Symbolic
- Zhausgr     +0.225 — Symbolic
- ZCU_AU      +0.407 — Social     ← dominant +ve loading
- Zamber      −0.239 — Social
- ZMonument   +0.204 — Social
- ZMort       +0.340 — Economic
- ZSichel     −0.149 — Economic
- ZBeil       −0.242 — Economic
- ZMW         +0.242 — Economic
- ZKeform     −0.353 — Cultural   ← strongest −ve loading
- Zkeverz     +0.382 — Cultural   ← strongest +ve loading

Sum-of-loadings per domain (oriented PC1): Symbolic +0.79, Social +0.37, Economic +0.19, Cultural +0.03 → PC1 is dominated by Symbolic, secondarily by Social & positive-loaded Economic, with Cultural nearly balanced due to Form–Decoration opposition.

Per-phase PC1 summary:
- Middle Neolithic (MN), BCE 3400–3000 (5 slices): n=5; PC1 mean = **−1.374**, median = −1.467, SD = 0.489, range [−1.783, −0.583]; **trend slope = −0.259 per century** (declining).
- Younger Neolithic (YN/SG), BCE 2900–2300 (7 slices): n=7; PC1 mean = **−1.117**, median = −1.214, SD = 0.430, range [−1.599, −0.412]; **trend slope = +0.120 per century** (rising).
- ΔPC1 (YN − MN) = **+0.257**.

Domain-mean Z values per phase:
- MN: Symbolic −0.085, Social +0.421, Cultural +0.436, Economic +0.204.
- YN: Symbolic −0.273, Social +0.010, Cultural −0.135, Economic +0.064. — every domain's mean is LOWER than MN's.

Per-variable contributions to the phase-mean PC1 (sample: drivers of ΔPC1 = +0.257, ordered by absolute size):
- +ZAmber collapse (MN peak → YN low): Δcontrib = **+0.417** (largest +ve mover of the MN→YN shift)
- +ZKeform decay: Δcontrib = **+0.228**
- +ZMonumentCount rise: Δcontrib = **+0.143**
- +Sickle emergence: Δcontrib = +0.042
- −Zkeverz decay: Δcontrib = −0.189
- −Zhausgr decay: Δcontrib = −0.178
- −ZMW decay: Δcontrib = −0.119
- −ZCU_AU decay: Δcontrib = −0.077
- (other terms < 0.05). Sum = +0.257 ✓.

Pollen openness × PC1 at the 12 BCE marks (supplementary):
- SMOOTH_MEAN_100y: Pearson **+0.477**, Spearman **+0.587**.
- Woserin_PC1_inter: Pearson +0.646, Spearman +0.720 (strongest).

Sanity check (`time_series_data.csv` `*_inter` projection vs centennial PC1 at 12 BCE marks):
- All 12 |PC1_proj − PC1_cent| ≤ 2.2 × 10⁻¹⁶ — the yearly interpolated values, after re-standardisation, project to exactly the centennial score, confirming that capital.csv is the canonical source of the centennial PCA.

### Hypothesis (natural-language answer)

A single joint PCA over the 12 Z-valued forms of capital at 39 hundred-year slices (BCE 4300–500) of `capital.csv` extracts a first principal component that explains **30.3 %** of the variance (PC1–PC3 cumulatively 62.7 %). After orienting PC1 so the sum of the 12 loadings is positive (greater overall capital → higher PC1), the axis is **bipolar** — Symbolic variables (Hatchets/Swords, Daggers, House-Size) dominate positively (Σ loadings = +0.79), joined by Copper-Gold, Monument-Count, Monument-Size, Depot and Pottery-Decoration as positive anchors, while **Amber, Pottery-Form, and Axes/Celts load negatively**; the Cultural domain therefore cancels out (Σ loadings = +0.03) because Pottery-Decoration (+0.38) and Pottery-Form (−0.35) straddle the axis.

On this axis the **Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE, 5 slices)** sits in the lower half of the centennial distribution at a mean PC1 of −1.37 (median −1.47; range −0.58 to −1.78) with a **falling within-phase trend of −0.26 PC1 units per century** — PC1 is highest at BCE 3400 (−0.58) and reaches the phase minimum at BCE 3000 (−1.78). MN therefore reads as a **"still-elevated but contracting"** phase: Social (+0.42) and Cultural (+0.44) domain means are at their centennial high, but the strong negative loadings on Amber and Pottery-Form — both peaking in MN — drive the composite down, and Symbolic is already slightly below zero.

The **Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE, 7 slices)** attains a *higher* PC1 (mean = −1.12; median −1.21; range −1.60 to −0.41) with a **rising within-phase trend of +0.12 PC1 units per century** — PC1 bottoms near BCE 2800 (−1.60) and recovers to −0.41 at BCE 2300, the local maximum of the two-phase window. YN is therefore best characterised as a **"recovering / re-accumulating" phase**, but the recovery is on PC1 only — every one of the four domain mean Z values is *lower* in YN than in MN (Symbolic −0.273 vs −0.085; Social +0.010 vs +0.421; Cultural −0.135 vs +0.436; Economic +0.064 vs +0.204). The rise in PC1 is the artefact of the bipolar loading structure: the **decline of the negative-loaded indicators Amber (Δ contribution +0.42) and Pottery-Form (+0.23) outweighs the decline of the positive-loaded Copper-Gold (−0.08), Pottery-Decoration (−0.19), House-Size (−0.18) and Monument-Size (−0.12)**, producing a *positive compositional shift* on PC1 even though raw capital indicators weaken on net.

The **inter-phase contrast ΔPC1 (YN − MN) = +0.26** is small in absolute terms (≈ a quarter of a centennial standard deviation) and is structurally driven by the *opposite-signed within-phase trends* (−0.26/century in MN vs +0.12/century in YN).

A supplementary cross-check against `pollen_openness_score_Belau_Woserin_Feeser_et_al_2019.csv` shows a moderate-to-strong positive monotonic coupling between PC1 and SMOOTH_MEAN_100y pollen openness at the 12 BCE marks (Pearson +0.48, Spearman **+0.59**) — i.e., the MN trough and the YN recovery in PC1 track the openness record, supporting the interpretation that the rising PC1 across the Younger Neolithic reflects a genuine composite-capital recovery co-temporal with landscape opening.

Caveats: (i) PC1 captures only 30 % of variance; PC2 (19.5 %, dominated by negative loadings on Amber, ZBeil, House-Size, Monument-Size, Pottery-Form) and PC3 (12.9 %) carry substantial additional domain-specific structure (esp. the Cultural Pottery-Form vs Pottery-Decoration opposition). (ii) `ZSichel` has input SD ≈ 0.54 — sub-unit variance — so its PC1 contribution is muted relative to its four peers in the Economic domain. (iii) The MN boundary at 3000 BCE and the YN start at 2900 BCE are already non-overlapping in `capital.csv`; the analysis is insensitive to the boundary convention because the data resolve it. (iv) Pollen openness is supplementary — it correlates with PC1 but is *not* part of the PCA. (v) Sensitivity to the correlation-vs-covariance choice is negligible (cov-PC1 explained variance 31.8 %, near-identical loadings).

### Limitations
- matplotlib is unavailable in this environment, so no PNG plots were produced. The four descriptive plots called for (PC1 timeline with phase shading, MN-vs-YN domain bars, PC1 loadings coloured by domain, PC1-vs-pollen scatter) are documented in `/workspace/artifacts/fix_and_plot.py` (saved but not executed) so the figures can be regenerated in any environment with matplotlib. All numerical evidence is present in the CSV/JSON artefacts.
- Single PCA over the full 4300–500 BCE window — by construction, PC1 loadings and centennial scores reflect the wider Bronze-Age trajectory, not only the MN/YN phases; the phase readings are correctly interpreted only relative to this broader series (the absolute score −1.37 / −1.12 is "low *for the centennial series*", not absolute capital).
- `time_series_data.csv`'s `*_inter` columns were used only for a sanity-check projection; they convey no additional PC1 information beyond the centennial values.

### Hypothesis (natural-language answer)

A single joint PCA over the 12 Z-valued forms of capital at 39 hundred-year slices (BCE 4300–500) of `capital.csv` extracts a first principal component that explains **30.3 %** of the variance (PC1–PC3 cumulatively 62.7 %). After orienting PC1 so the sum of the 12 loadings is positive (greater overall capital → higher PC1), the axis is **bipolar** — Symbolic variables (Hatchets/Swords, Daggers, House-Size) dominate positively (Σ loadings = +0.79), joined by Copper-Gold, Monument-Count, Monument-Size, Depot and Pottery-Decoration as positive anchors, while **Amber, Pottery-Form, and Axes/Celts load negatively**; the Cultural domain therefore cancels out (Σ loadings = +0.03) because Pottery-Decoration (+0.38) and Pottery-Form (−0.35) straddle the axis.

On this axis the **Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE, 5 slices)** sits in the lower half of the centennial distribution at a mean PC1 of −1.37 (median −1.47; range −0.58 to −1.78) with a **falling within-phase trend of −0.26 PC1 units per century** — PC1 is highest at BCE 3400 (−0.58) and reaches the phase minimum at BCE 3000 (−1.78). MN therefore reads as a **"still-elevated but contracting"** phase: Social (+0.42) and Cultural (+0.44) domain means are at their centennial high, but the strong negative loadings on Amber and Pottery-Form — both peaking in MN — drive the composite down, and Symbolic is already slightly below zero.

The **Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE, 7 slices)** attains a *higher* PC1 (mean = −1.12; median −1.21; range −1.60 to −0.41) with a **rising within-phase trend of +0.12 PC1 units per century** — PC1 bottoms near BCE 2800 (−1.60) and recovers to −0.41 at BCE 2300, the local maximum of the two-phase window. YN is therefore best characterised as a **"recovering / re-accumulating" phase**, but the recovery is on PC1 only — every one of the four domain mean Z values is *lower* in YN than in MN (Symbolic −0.273 vs −0.085; Social +0.010 vs +0.421; Cultural −0.135 vs +0.436; Economic +0.064 vs +0.204). The rise in PC1 is the artefact of the bipolar loading structure: the **decline of the negative-loaded indicators Amber (Δ contribution +0.42) and Pottery-Form (+0.23) outweighs the decline of the positive-loaded Copper-Gold (−0.08), Pottery-Decoration (−0.19), House-Size (−0.18) and Monument-Size (−0.12)**, producing a *positive compositional shift* on PC1 even though raw capital indicators weaken on net.

The **inter-phase contrast ΔPC1 (YN − MN) = +0.26** is small in absolute terms (≈ a quarter of a centennial standard deviation) and is structurally driven by the *opposite-signed within-phase trends* (−0.26/century in MN vs +0.12/century in YN).

(iii) The MN boundary at 3000 BCE and the YN start at 2900 BCE are already non-overlapping in `capital.csv`; the analysis is insensitive to the boundary convention because the data resolve it. (iv) Pollen openness is supplementary — it correlates with PC1 but is *not* part of the PCA. (v) Sensitivity to the correlation-vs-covariance choice is negligible (cov-PC1 explained variance 31.8 %, near-identical loadings).

native_result.query: In the PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices, during the Younger Bronze Age (1100-500 BCE), how does the principal component value of PC1 in the beginning of the period at 1100 BCE differ from the subsequent time horizons between 1000 to 500 BCE?
native_result.HypoA: The beginning of the Younger Bronze Age (1100 BCE) is associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1), while the majority of time horizons (1000-500 BCE) are characterized by positive values on PC1. This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: In the PCA on the 12 forms of capital (HatchetSword, Dagger, HouseSize, CopperGold, Amber, MonumentCount, Depot, Sickle, Axes&Celts, MonumentSize, PotteryForm, PotteryDecoration) computed per 100-year time slice over the Younger Bronze Age (1100-500 BCE), the PC1 score at the start of the period (BCE 1100) lies outside the [min, max] range of the six subsequent BCE 1000-500 horizons, on the side away from the central tendency of those later bins - i.e. PC1(1100) is the single most extreme economic-capital-positive reading of the Younger Bronze Age, and the magnitude of the gap (|PC1(1100) - PC1(t)|) tends to grow from BCE 1000 to BCE 500 (with a small local contraction at BCE 800). In the PCA-full run (fit on all 39 rows x 12 capital Z-features, projected to 7 YBA rows), PC1(1100) = -4.51 versus subsequent range [-2.18, -0.79]; in the PCA-YBA-only run (fit on 7 rows x 10 features after dropping ZSichel and ZKeform as zero-variance), PC1(1100) = +5.78 versus [-2.27, -0.03]; sign-flip rule kept the loadings of PC1 on ZCU_AU, ZAmber, ZHort and Zhausgr positively aligned. The Belau pollen openness score (Feeser et al. 2019), where available (BCE 1100-700), is positively correlated with PC1_full (r = +0.69) and negatively with PC1_ybaonly (r = -0.60); this is supporting context, not a PCA feature, and pollen data do not exist for BCE 600 and 500.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded capital.csv and pollen_openness_score_Belau_Woserin_Feeser_et_al_2019.csv with decimal=','. (a) PCA-full: fit SVD on the 39x12 globally-Z-standardised matrix (no zero-variance columns at full scale) and projected the 7 YBA rows through that rotation (raw PC1 variance ratio 0.3033). (b) PCA-YBA-only: filtered YBA rows, dropped ZSichel and ZKeform (zero variance within YBA), re-standardised on the 7x10 matrix, SVD fit (PC1 variance ratio 0.6253). For both runs, the same sign-flip rule was applied: keep PC1 sign unflipped only when loadings on {ZCU_AU, ZAmber, ZHort, Zhausgr} are all positive; otherwise negate PC1. PCA-YBA-only satisfied the rule directly; PCA-full required a single flip. Score tables and PC1(1100) - PC1(t) diff tables were written for both. Verdict: PC1(1100) is OUTSIDE the [min, max] of {PC1(1000..500)} in both runs - BELOW in PCA-full, ABOVE in PCA-YBA-only, both on the economic-capital-positive side. Pollen context: Belau_PC1_inter centroid mean per YBA bin was correlated with PC1 at the 5 overlapping horizons BCE 1100..700; BCE 600 and 500 acknowledged as missing. NATURAL-LANGUAGE HYPOTHESIS (answer to the question)
────────────────────────────────────
During the Younger Bronze Age (YBA, 1100–500 BCE), the principal component value of PC1 at the beginning of the period (1100 BCE) is dramatically higher and of opposite sign from every subsequent 100-year horizon between 1000 and 500 BCE.

• Direction & sign. The canonicalised PC1 score at 1100 BCE is +5.35 (positive, large), while every other YBA slice has a negative PC1 score: -0.03 (1000 BCE), -0.26 (900 BCE), -0.14 (800 BCE), -0.96 (700 BCE), -1.86 (600 BCE) and -2.10 (500 BCE). All six contrasts therefore have a negative sign — 1100 BCE is unambiguously “on the positive side” of PC1, every later slice is on the negative side.

• Magnitude. Δ(t) = score(t) − score(1100 BCE) ranges from −5.38 (1000 BCE) to −7.45 (500 BCE), i.e. 1100 BCE lies ≈5–7½ PC1 units above the rest of the YBA region. The combined PC1+PC2 variance explained is 85.8 % (PC1: 62.5 %, PC2: 23.2 %), so PC1 captures a clearly one-dimensional “overall capital intensity” axis: PC1 has positive loadings on eight of the ten active forms of capital (Zhouse-size +0.39, Zdagger +0.39, Zmonument +0.38, ZCU/AU +0.37, Zambber +0.34, Zhort +0.30, Zhatchet/Sword +0.22, ZMW +0.14) and only negative loadings on Zbeil (−0.08) and Zkeverz (−0.38).

• Trend across 1000–500 BCE. After the high point at 1100 BCE, PC1 crashes by ~5.4 units already at 1000 BCE (essentially to the window's zero-line), wobbles slightly (small rebound at 800 BCE), then declines monotonically through 700, 600 and 500 BCE. In other words, relative to 1100 BCE, all subsequent YBA slices are below PC1, and the absolute level of PC1 trends downward towards the end of the Younger Bronze Age.

• Cross-validation. A companion PCA on the full 39 × 12 matrix (which keeps the constant ZSichel/ZKeform because they vary outside YBA) reproduces the same direction: aligned PC1 = +4.45 at 1100 BCE and falls through +2.15 (1000), +1.63 (900), +1.89 (800), +1.23 (700), +0.80 (600) and +0.78 (500). The 1100 BCE slice is the highest, 500 BCE the lowest, and the entire 1000–500 BCE block sits below 1100 BCE on PC1.

────────────────────────────────────
1. Loaded /workspace/data/capital.csv with the csv module, replacing German-locale decimal commas (",") inside quoted Z cells with "." so the 12 Z-value variables parse as floats. Dropped the metadata-flagged "group" and "color" columns.
2. Confirmed 39 rows on an exact 100-year BCE grid (500…4300); filtered to the Younger Bronze Age = 7 rows (1100, 1000, 900, 800, 700, 600, 500 BCE). Note: the question text says "13 Z values"; the file (and datasets.json) actually contain 12, so the analysis uses 12.
3. Within YBA, dropped ZSichel (≡0) and ZKeform (≡−1.13) which have zero variance and therefore cannot contribute to PCA in this window. The active PCA matrix is 7 × 10.
4. Standardised the 7 columns by their YBA sample mean and std (equivalent to using the correlation matrix; chosen because YBA-window per-column sd ranges from 0 (dropped) to 1.49 (ZHort), so a covariance PCA would be dominated by ZHort and ZCU_AU).

native_result.HypoB:
**Hypothesis (data-grounded, primary = all-12 PCA, supporting = symbolic-only PCA on PC2 structure).**

In the PCA run on the 12 standardized Z-variables across the 39 hundred-year slices of `data/capital.csv` (PC1 = 30.33 %, PC2 = 19.47 %; cumulative PC1+PC2 = 49.79 %), the three symbolic-capital variables — hatchets/swords (ZAxtSchwert), daggers (ZDolch), and house size (Zhausgr) — load **uniformly positive on PC1** with similar small-to-moderate magnitudes (ZAxtSchwert +0.299 [bootstrap 95 % CI +0.050, +0.499]; ZDolch +0.266 [+0.020, +0.444]; Zhausgr +0.225 [−0.187, +0.393]), ranking 5th–7th by |PC1| behind ZCU_AU (+0.407), Zkeverz (+0.382), ZKeform (−0.353), ZHort (+0.340). They therefore co-move with the dominant axis of overall capital accumulation rather than defining it on their own. Across PC2 the symbolic triad is **NOT uniformly distributed**: Zhausgr carries a meaningful positive loading (+0.327; bootstrap mean +0.192, CI [−0.355, +0.561]), whereas ZAxtSchwert (+0.054; bootstrap mean +0.008, CI [−0.324, +0.348]) and ZDolch (+0.074; bootstrap mean +0.001, CI [−0.606, +0.487]) sit close to zero. Within symbolic capital, **house-size is the dimension that varies independently of the dominant axis**, while weapons (daggers, hatchets/swords) co-vary with the rest of the capital bundle on PC2. This internal PC2 split is corroborated by the supporting symbolic-only PCA restricted to the three variables (PC1 = 54.40 %, PC2 = 28.84 %, cumulative 83.23 %), where PC2 cleanly opposes ZAxtSchwert (+0.791) to Zhausgr (−0.609) and leaves ZDolch (−0.063) effectively orthogonal — the same qualitative pattern. **Caveat:** bootstrap 95 % CIs on the symbolic triad's PC2 loadings are wide, so magnitudes should not be over-interpreted, but the *sign pattern and relative ranking on PC2 are stable* across both the all-12 PCA and the symbolic-only sensitivity analysis.

**Workflow (5 lines).**
1. Load `data/capital.csv` with `decimal=','`, drop `group`/`color`, keep BCE; assemble the 39 BCE-aligned 100-year slices × 12 Z-variables (capital.csv is already 100-year-binned — no re-binning required).
2. Standardize each Z-column to mean 0, std 1 (ddof=1); run PCA via `numpy.linalg.svd` on the centered/scaled matrix (sklearn-equivalent for the correlation matrix).
3. Orient signs deterministically — PC1 to positive on ZAxtSchwert, PC2 to positive on argmax-|PC2 loading| (ZBeil); report both raw and oriented loadings in `artifacts/loadings.csv` and `artifacts/loadings_full.json`.
4. Bootstrap B=1000 slice-row resamples (seed 20260525); 2.5/97.5 percentile CIs on the symbolic triad's PC1/PC2 loadings in `artifacts/bootstrap_CIs.csv`.
5. Sensitivities: (a) PCA on raw Z (without re-standardization); (b) symbolic-only PCA on ZAxtSchwert/ZDolch/Zhausgr alone. SVG figures `artifacts/biplot.svg`, `artifacts/loadings_barplot.svg`, `artifacts/scree.svg`. Executed notebook `artifacts/analysis.ipynb`.

In the PCA run on the 12 standardized Z-variables across the 39 hundred-year slices of `data/capital.csv` (PC1 = 30.33 %, PC2 = 19.47 %; cumulative PC1+PC2 = 49.79 %), the three symbolic-capital variables — hatchets/swords (ZAxtSchwert), daggers (ZDolch), and house size (Zhausgr) — load **uniformly positive on PC1** with similar small-to-moderate magnitudes (ZAxtSchwert +0.299 [bootstrap 95 % CI +0.050, +0.499]; ZDolch +0.266 [+0.020, +0.444]; Zhausgr +0.225 [−0.187, +0.393]), ranking 5th–7th by |PC1| behind ZCU_AU (+0.407), Zkeverz (+0.382), ZKeform (−0.353), ZHort (+0.340). They therefore co-move with the dominant axis of overall capital accumulation rather than defining it on their own. Across PC2 the symbolic triad is **NOT uniformly distributed**: Zhausgr carries a meaningful positive loading (+0.327; bootstrap mean +0.192, CI [−0.355, +0.561]), whereas ZAxtSchwert (+0.054; bootstrap mean +0.008, CI [−0.324, +0.348]) and ZDolch (+0.074; bootstrap mean +0.001, CI [−0.606, +0.487]) sit close to zero. Within symbolic capital, **house-size is the dimension that varies independently of the dominant axis**, while weapons (daggers, hatchets/swords) co-vary with the rest of the capital bundle on PC2. This internal PC2 split is corroborated by the supporting symbolic-only PCA restricted to the three variables (PC1 = 54.40 %, PC2 = 28.84 %, cumulative 83.23 %), where PC2 cleanly opposes ZAxtSchwert (+0.791) to Zhausgr (−0.609) and leaves ZDolch (−0.063) effectively orthogonal — the same qualitative pattern. **Caveat:** bootstrap 95 % CIs on the symbolic triad's PC2 loadings are wide, so magnitudes should not be over-interpreted, but the *sign pattern and relative ranking on PC2 are stable* across both the all-12 PCA and the symbolic-only sensitivity analysis.

**Workflow (5 lines).**
1. Load `data/capital.csv` with `decimal=','`, drop `group`/`color`, keep BCE; assemble the 39 BCE-aligned 100-year slices × 12 Z-variables (capital.csv is already 100-year-binned — no re-binning required).
2. Standardize each Z-column to mean 0, std 1 (ddof=1); run PCA via `numpy.linalg.svd` on the centered/scaled matrix (sklearn-equivalent for the correlation matrix).
3. Orient signs deterministically — PC1 to positive on ZAxtSchwert, PC2 to positive on argmax-|PC2 loading| (ZBeil); report both raw and oriented loadings in `artifacts/loadings.csv` and `artifacts/loadings_full.json`.
4. Bootstrap B=1000 slice-row resamples (seed 20260525); 2.5/97.5 percentile CIs on the symbolic triad's PC1/PC2 loadings in `artifacts/bootstrap_CIs.csv`.
5. Sensitivities: (a) PCA on raw Z (without re-standardization); (b) symbolic-only PCA on ZAxtSchwert/ZDolch/Zhausgr alone. SVG figures `artifacts/biplot.svg`, `artifacts/loadings_barplot.svg`, `artifacts/scree.svg`. Executed notebook `artifacts/analysis.ipynb`.

**Artifacts (workspace-relative):**
- `artifacts/analysis.ipynb` (executed; 4 cells: intro markdown, code cell with embedded stdout, results markdown, run-log markdown; 36574 B)
- `artifacts/scripts/run_capital_pca.py` (the runnable script; 22763 B), mirrored at `scripts/run_capital_pca.py`
- `artifacts/loadings.csv` (full 12-var raw+oriented loadings)
- `artifacts/loadings_full.json` (full structured results including sensitivities and bootstrap CIs)
- `artifacts/explained_variance.csv` (PC1..PC12, eigenvalues, ratios, cumulative)
- `artifacts/bootstrap_CIs.csv` (symbolic triad PC1/PC2 mean + 2.5/97.5 CIs)
- `artifacts/biplot.svg`, `artifacts/loadings_barplot.svg`, `artifacts/scree.svg` (all validated as well-formed XML)
- `artifacts/run_log.txt` (full textual console report including ASCII barplots)

**Limitations to note in the final answer:** n=39 yields wide PC2 bootstrap CIs; the symbolic triad does *not* dominate PC1 in the full PCA (it rides a broader capital-accumulation vector topped by ZCU_AU/Zkeverz/ZKeform/ZHort); in the 12-var PCA, PC2 is dominated by ZBeil/Zamber/ZMW/ZKeform/ZMonument, so the symbolic triad's PC2 signal is diluted in that setting and only emerges cleanly when the symbolic triad is isolated.

Counter to an expectation of cross-symbol synchrony, monument counts and axes co-rise while the two weapon-symbol components stay flat and HouseSize declines \u2014 a co-trajectory of the built form with the axe/celt record that is decoupled from, and partly opposed to, the Hatchet-Swords / Daggers / HouseSize reading of symbolic capital. Monument size (ZMonumentSize / ZMW) moves opposite to the count (Pearson r \u2248 \u22120.20 vs ZMonument, r \u2248 \u22120.62 vs ZBeil), so the BCE 3200 spike is one of more, but not larger, monuments. As backdrop the pollen-based openness record (Belau PC1, the cross-site MEAN, and SMOOTH_MEAN_100y) rises across the slice (Belau_PC1_inter \u22121.16 \u2192 +1.65; MEAN \u22121.86 \u2192 +0.08; SMOOTH_MEAN_100y \u22121.81 \u2192 +0.20), so the monument-and-axes peak at BCE 3200 sits on a backdrop of rising, not falling, openness.

This is the only centennial transition with declining Form and increasing Decoration across the stated BCE 4300 → BCE 500 horizon, with both raw datasets identifying BCE 1700 and agreeing to two decimal places.

The diagnostic transition is BCE 1800 → BCE 1700, identified as Late Neolithic (LN).

### Final natural-language hypothesis (data-grounded, ready to submit)

**The summed social-capital index SC3 = Z(CuAu) + Z(Amber) + Z(MonumentCount) peaks in the 14th century BCE**, as a two-bin plateau in capital.csv (rows BCE = 1400 and BCE = 1300, both tied at SC3 = +4.24σ). Per the approved reporting convention this is the **14th century BCE, bin center ≈ 1400 BCE, window 1500–1300 BCE, phase = Older Bronze Age (OBA)**, equivalent Common-Era framing ≈ 1400 BCE / ~3350 BP / ~3300 cal BP (`calBP = 1950 − CE_year`). The peak sits +6.10σ above the prior trough (BCE 2000/1900, Late Neolithic, SC3 ≈ −1.86σ), a per-component mean lift of ≈ +2.0σ.

**All three headline components rose into the peak across the 2-bin (~200 y) lead window preceding it** (BCE 1600 and 1500 → BCE 1400 plateau), but the magnitudes are very different:

| Component | Z at lead-window mean (BCE 1600, 1500) | Z at peak bin (BCE 1400/1300, OBA) | ΔZ over lead | Verdict | Component's own absolute peak |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Cu/Au** | −0.36 | +2.54 | **+2.90σ** | **ROSE — strong** | BCE 1200 (CE_center −1150), OBA, Z = +2.85 |
| **MonumentCount** | +0.17 | +1.71 | **+1.54σ** | **ROSE — strong** | BCE 2700 (CE_center −2650), SG, Z = +3.95 |
| **Amber** | −0.38 | −0.01 | **+0.37σ** | ROSE — only marginal stabilisation | BCE 3300 (CE_center −3250), MN, Z = +1.54 (Amber's overall maximum had been much earlier) |
| MonumentSize (sensitivity only) | +0.64 | +0.60 | −0.03σ | flat / slightly declined | BCE 3100, MN, Z = +0.68 |

So the headline social-capital peak in the 14th century BCE is **driven primarily by the contemporaneous acceleration in Copper-and-Gold artifacts and MonumentCount**; Amber contributes only a marginal stabilisation off its Late Neolithic/LN-YBA low (its own much larger peak was in the Middle Neolithic, BCE 3300). The window preceding the peak was Amber-suppressed; the rise into the peak is dominated by metals and monuments, with amber tagging along weakly.

**Openness cross-check (one-line, supporting context only):** pollen-based openness (Belau_PC1_inter, SMOOTH_MEAN_100y) is **rising** through the peak century (Belau_PC1_inter +1.15 in the prior century → +1.82 at the peak; MEAN +0.79 → +2.16), consistent with the broader Holocene connectivity uptrend but NOT itself part of the social-capital definition.

**Robustness / sensitivities (artifacts only — not the headline):**
- `SC_mean_3 = SC3 / 3` argmax CE = −1350 (same), value = +1.41σ.
- `SC_4 = SC3 + ZMonumentSize` argmax CE = −1350 (same), value = +4.90σ.
- Within-phase-detrended `SC3_dt` argmax CE = −1050 (Late OBA / early YBA — OBA phase mean already carries much of the rise); same plateau region.

- The three capital.csv leading rows BCE ∈ {4300, 4200, 4100} carry identical Z-values (prefilled/empty envelope) and were excluded from the active-data trough search; they do not affect the headline peak.
- capital.csv BCE = 500 has `ZMW = 0` as a sentinel; because headline SC3 excludes MonumentSize, this does not affect the SC3 series.
- Pollen data (`pollen_openness_*.csv`) stops at CE −702; openness cross-check uses `pollen_inter` from `time_series_data.csv` for the last bins.

### Workflow (executed end-to-end on supplied data)

1. Loaded `data/capital.csv`, `data/time_series_data.csv`, and `data/pollen_openness_score_Belau_Woserin_Feeser_et_al_2019.csv` (German decimal-comma fix via `decimal=','`).

3. Cross-checked by aggregating `CopperGold_inter`, `Amber_inter`, `MonumentCount_inter`, `MonumentSize_inter` from `time_series_data.csv` annual series into identical 100y CE bins; argmax is identical (CE_center = −1350, value = +4.24σ).

6. Identified prior trough on active (non-prefilled) data: BCE 2000/1900, Late Neolithic, SC3 = −1.86σ → ΔSC3_trough_to_peak = +6.10σ.
7. Computed per-component ΔZ over the 2-bin lead window (BCE 1600, 1500) before the peak plateau; tabulated `rose_into_peak` and individual component peaks/centuries.

**Composite definition (study context):** `social_capital = ZCU_AU + Zamber + ZMonument`.

(F) NATURAL-LANGUAGE HYPOTHESIS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Summed social capital (ZCU_AU + Zamber + ZMonument) peaked in the 14th century BCE (1400–1301
BCE; CE −1400..−1301), in the middle of the OBA cultural period. The peak value of the
3-component summed index is +4.24 (relative to a per-component z-score baseline of μ≈0, σ≈1
across 3,601 per-year Z records spanning 4100–500 BCE). The peak is robust under three of four
sensitivity variants — mean-of-12, clipped-negative SC3, and the default *_inter sum all
select K=14; only the raw-Z-at-bin-center variant breaks the strict tie between K=14 and
K=13 by returning K=13, an artifact of the warmer Amber (Zamber) tied at −0.01 across the two
bins and of the linear interpolation’s smoothing across them.

The 14th-century BCE capital peak is driven primarily by Copper+Gold (ZCU_AU = +2.54, the
all-time high for that series) and Monument Count (ZMonument = +1.71, top-3 of its series),
with Amber essentially flat at its long-run baseline (Zamber = −0.01, NOT rising into the
peak; it in fact declines monotonically from K=15 through K=12, from −0.08 → −0.01 →
−0.29 → −0.58). Beyond the SC3 trio, two further individual social-capital components
clearly RISE INTO this peak: HatchetSword (ZAxtSchwert = +2.61; second-highest in its 37-bin
record, top-3 series) and Dagger (ZDolch = +1.68; rank-3 in its series). MonumentSize
(ZMW = +0.64) also qualifies on the dual criterion (above long-run mean AND top-3 of its
series), and so the peak is a coherent weaponry-and-monumentality spike — high-value bronze
tools (HatchetSword, Dagger) and high monument counts/sizes occur simultaneously with
concentrated copper/gold deposition. The remaining components (HouseSize, Depot, Sickle,
AxesCelts, PotteryForm, PotteryDecoration) are decisively NOT co-peaking: most are below
their long-run means and the rest fail the top-3-of-series test.

Supporting demographic evidence from pollen_inter_100 (Belau/Woserin PC1 mean, 100-year
rolling) places the 14th-century BCE bin at +1.48 (rolling mean, positive regime) and the
adjacent 13th-century BCE bin at +2.04 — i.e., openness is high and rising through the OBA
peak, but pollen is itself still climbing toward its all-time window maximum in the latest
centuries (~+8.7 in the 6th–5th century BCE), so it is a corroborating rather than a
co-locating signal.

BOTTOM LINE:  In the 14th century BCE (1400–1301 BCE), summed social capital reached its peak
of +4.24 in the data window (4100–500 BCE); this peak is driven by Copper+Gold and
Monument Count within the SC3 trio, plus a wider cluster of rising individual components —
HatchetSword (+2.61), Dagger (+1.68), MonumentSize (+0.64) — representing a clear Bronze-Age
(OBA) co-spike of precious-metal deposition, monumental construction, and high-value bronze
weaponry.

BCE; CE −1400..−1301), in the middle of the OBA cultural period. The peak value of the
3-component summed index is +4.24 (relative to a per-component z-score baseline of μ≈0, σ≈1
across 3,601 per-year Z records spanning 4100–500 BCE). The peak is robust under three of four
sensitivity variants — mean-of-12, clipped-negative SC3, and the default *_inter sum all
select K=14; only the raw-Z-at-bin-center variant breaks the strict tie between K=14 and
K=13 by returning K=13, an artifact of the warmer Amber (Zamber) tied at −0.01 across the two
bins and of the linear interpolation’s smoothing across them.

all-time high for that series) and Monument Count (ZMonument = +1.71, top-3 of its series),

series), and so the peak is a coherent weaponry-and-monumentality spike — high-value bronze
tools (HatchetSword, Dagger) and high monument counts/sizes occur simultaneously with
concentrated copper/gold deposition. The remaining components (HouseSize, Depot, Sickle,
AxesCelts, PotteryForm, PotteryDecoration) are decisively NOT co-peaking: most are below
their long-run means and the rest fail the top-3-of-series test.

Supporting demographic evidence from pollen_inter_100 (Belau/Woserin PC1 mean, 100-year
rolling) places the 14th-century BCE bin at +1.48 (rolling mean, positive regime) and the
adjacent 13th-century BCE bin at +2.04 — i.e., openness is high and rising through the OBA
peak, but pollen is itself still climbing toward its all-time window maximum in the latest
centuries (~+8.7 in the 6th–5th century BCE), so it is a corroborating rather than a
co-locating signal.

BOTTOM LINE:  In the 14th century BCE (1400–1301 BCE), summed social capital reached its peak
of +4.24 in the data window (4100–500 BCE); this peak is driven by Copper+Gold and
Monument Count within the SC3 trio, plus a wider cluster of rising individual components —
HatchetSword (+2.61), Dagger (+1.68), MonumentSize (+0.64) — representing a clear Bronze-Age
(OBA) co-spike of precious-metal deposition, monumental construction, and high-value bronze
weaponry.

native_result.query: How does the prevalence of non-native plants introduced via gardening vary based on habitat type?
native_result.HypoA: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats.
native_result.HypoB: In the Catalonia study region, the prevalence of non-native plant species introduced via the gardening pathway varies steeply by habitat — it is highest in low-elevation, anthropogenically disturbed habitats close to roads and human settlements, peaking in Wetlands (50.0% of plots, 95% bootstrap CI 34.2–65.8%), Urban (47.7% [35.4–60.0%]), Coastal (44.8% [27.6–62.1%]), and Riparian (36.1% [24.6–47.5%]), and falling to near-zero in Rock outcrops (0%), Scrublands (1.9% [0.0–4.7%]), and forest interiors (Broad-leaved 4.4%, Coniferous 6.5%). Hurdle-binomial odds-ratios relative to the Croplands baseline (20.7% prevalence [12.0–29.3%]) are 3.84× for Wetlands, 3.50× for Urban, 3.12× for Coastal and 2.17× for Riparian (all BH-FDR q≤0.05); forests and Scrublands drop to 0.07–0.27× odds. The environmental gradient consistent with the ornamental-escape mechanism is dominated by elevation (odds ratio 0.10 per SD increase in elevation, q=0.0008) and proximity to roads (OR 0.68 per SD increase in distance-to-road, q=0.043), with the urban-vs-cropland buffer context collapsing to a non-significant PC1 once elevation is controlled. Stacked-composition analysis shows that when non-native species do occur they are dominated by gardening origin in lowland habitats (53–100% of non-native richness in Wetlands / Coastal / Coniferous / Broad-leaved forests) but not in Urban (29.8% gardening, 68.9% unintentional) or Croplands (18.5% gardening, 76.9% unintentional) where unintentional escape remains the leading driver. A supplementary phylogenetic-distance analysis suggests pathway categories are phylogenetically clustered (Mantel-style K=0.957, p=0.004, B=5000 permutations over 81 matched tips), but this does not drive the habitat-level hypothesis.
native_result.WorkflowB: Step 0 — n.total semantics: row-wise check that n.total == n.gard + n.unint + n.agfo (passed in 632/632 rows, Case A, so share_d == dominance_d). Step 1 — per-habitat prevalence, conditional share, and abundance-weighted dominance with B=5000 nonparametric bootstrap CIs at the plot level (low-n habitats flagged with explicit CIs). Step 2 — hurdle model with Croplands as reference: (a) binomial (logit) presence model with BH-FDR over 9 habitat coefficients (LLR p ≈ 4e-27, pseudo-R²=0.243); (b) zero-truncated Poisson count model (manual scipy implementation over n.gard>0, n=117 plots) with paired Poisson GLM with HC1 robust SE as a stability fallback (dispersion=1.14, Poisson adequate). Step 3 — env correlates: VIF check on 7 env predictors; PCA1 collapse of (urban.2009.500m, cropland.2009.500m) imposed (Urban=+0.84, Cropland=-0.55, 54% var) per protocol even though the VIF for that pair was ~1; remaining elevation/temperature/rainfall collinearity documented but not collapsed beyond protocol. Logit-LM on z-scored env predictors + BH-FDR q=0.05 across 9 coefs; joint habitat+env regularized logit (alpha=0.1) due to singular Hessian at full MLE. Step 4 — figure/data exports as CSV (matplotlib unavailable); ASCII bar visualisations embedded in ANALYSIS_REPORT.md. Step 5 — phylogenetic signal: custom Newick parser (biopython unavailable), 81/81 tips matched; K-clustering Mantel-style surrogate for Pagel's λ. native_result.HypoB: The prevalence of non-native plants introduced via the Gardening pathway varies systematically across habitat types in the Barcelona province. Region-wide it averages about a third (Σn.gard/Σn.total ≈ 0.35, 169/481 occurrences across 191 non-zero of 632 plots), and the pathway-by-habitat contingency is clearly non-random (χ² = 75.2, df = 18, p ≈ 5.8×10⁻⁹, Cramér's V ≈ 0.28). The pattern is a contrast, not a single winner: Gardening prevalence is low and Unintentional-dominated in intensively human-managed habitats — Croplands (prev_gard ≈ 0.19, 95% CI 0.12–0.27, N=108), Urban (≈ 0.30, 0.23–0.38, N=151), and Rock outcrops (0.00 but N=1, fragile) — and substantially higher in urban-adjacent semi-natural habitats where Gardening becomes the leading pathway: Wetlands (≈ 0.56, 0.42–0.68, N=52), Coastal (≈ 0.54, 0.39–0.67, N=43), with Riparian (≈ 0.37, 0.28–0.46, N=96) and Meadows (≈ 0.31 but N=13) at the regional mean. Data-sparse habitats (Broad-leaved forests 1.00 at N=4, Coniferous forests 0.88 at N=8, Scrublands 0.40 at N=5, Rock outcrops 0.00 at N=1) are retained but their proportions should be treated as fragile. Contextually, the region's temporal trends show Gardening-origin introductions growing from 18 (pre-1500) to 397 (1985–2019; ≈75% of the period's introductions), consistent with gardening-escape pressure increasingly reaching semi-natural habitats such as Wetlands and Coastal sites.

## Resultado del análisis (etapa result)

### Hipótesis grounded (respuesta a la pregunta)

"La prevalencia de plantas no nativas introducidas vía jardinería varía fuerte y significativamente entre tipos de hábitat en la provincia de Barcelona. Sobre los 632 plots y 481 registros no nativos (169 jardín, 289 involuntaria, 23 AgriForest), χ²(18) = 75.20, p = 5.83·10⁻⁹, Cramér's V = 0.28; contraste focal jardín vs resto χ²(9) = 48.83, p = 1.79·10⁻⁷, V = 0.32. La proporción agregada de jardín dentro del total no nativo del hábitat (Σ n.gard/Σ n.total) es máxima en los hábitats húmedos y costeros — Humedales 55.8 % (IC95 % bootstrap = 41.1-73.2 %; Firth OR vs Urbano = 2.94, p = 0.0011) y Costero 53.5 % (37.8-68.8 %; OR = 2.68, p = 0.0052) — intermedia en Ripario 36.5 % (26.7-47.3 %), Urbano 29.8 % y Cultivos 18.5 % (12.8-24.8 %), y exploratoriamente alta en Bosques de coníferas 87.5 % (Σ = 8 registros, Firth OR = 11.7, p = 0.011). Los Cultivos son el único hábitat donde la vía involuntaria (76.9 %) supera dominante a la jardinería. Los contrastes pareados ajustados por Benjamini-Hochberg destacan Wetlands vs Croplands (p_BH = 0.0002), Coastal vs Croplands (p_BH = 0.0006), Wetlands vs Urban (p_BH = 0.011), Coastal vs Urban (p_BH = 0.024), Riparian vs Croplands (p_BH = 0.024) y Coniferous vs Urban (p_BH = 0.043). El GLM binomial-negativo con offset log(n.total) y covariables (elevación, uso urbano/cultivo 2009 a 500 m, distancia a carretera, temperatura) replica el patrón (las covariables apenas añaden información más allá del hábitat; LRT ΔLL = 2.91, gl = 5, p = 0.713). El análisis de sensibilidad restringido a los seis hábitats con Σ n.total ≥ 10 mantiene la asociación (χ²(5) = 31.42, p = 7.74·10⁻⁶, V = 0.26) y el mismo ranking (Wetlands > Cultivos, Coastal > Cultivos, etc.). En síntesis, la presencia de la jardinería como vía de invasión es máxima en hábitats húmedos y costeros, intermedia en urbanos y mínima en cultivos; los bosques densos muestran una señal Jardín muy alta pero con muy pocos registros, por lo que su conclusión debe etiquetarse como exploratoria."
